title: Block diagonal matrix
statementMd:
Implement a unitary operation on $N$ qubits which is represented by a square matrix of size $2^N$ which has 2x2 blocks of non-zero elements on the main diagonal and zero elements everywhere else.

For example, for $N = 3$ the matrix of the operation should have the following shape:

```
XX......
XX......
..XX....
..XX....
....XX..
....XX..
......XX
......XX
```

Here `X` denotes a "non-zero" element of the matrix (a complex number which has the square of the absolute value greater than or equal to $10^{-5}$), and `.` denotes a "zero" element of the matrix (a complex number which has the square of the absolute value less than $10^{-5}$).

The row and column indices of the matrix follow little endian format: the least significant bit of the index is stored first in the qubit array. Thus, the first column of the matrix gives you the coefficients of the basis states you'll get if you apply the unitary to the $|00..0\rangle$ basis state, the second column - to the $|10..0\rangle$ basis state etc. You can use the [DumpUnitary tool](https://github.com/Microsoft/QuantumKatas/tree/master/utilities/DumpUnitary) to get the coefficients of the matrix your unitary implements (up to relative phases between columns) and the corresponding pattern of `X`s and `.`s.

You have to implement an operation which takes an array of $N$ ($2 \le N \le 5$) qubits as an input and applies the unitary transformation with the matrix of the described shape to it. If there are multiple unitaries which satisfy the requirements, you can implement any of them. The "output" of your operation is the pattern of the matrix coefficients implemented by it; you can see the testing harness in the [UnitaryPatterns](https://github.com/Microsoft/QuantumKatas/tree/master/UnitaryPatterns) kata.

Your code should have the following signature:

```
namespace Solution {
    open Microsoft.Quantum.Primitive;
    open Microsoft.Quantum.Canon;

    operation Solve (qs : Qubit[]) : Unit {
        // your code here
    }
}
```

You are not allowed to use measurements in your operation.
statementZhMd:
实现一个作用于 $N$ 个量子比特的酉操作。该操作由一个大小为 $2^N$ 的方阵表示，该方阵的主对角线上为 $2\times2$ 的非零元素块，其他位置均为零元素。

例如，当 $N = 3$ 时，该操作的矩阵应具有如下形状：

```
XX......
XX......
..XX....
..XX....
....XX..
....XX..
......XX
......XX
```

这里，`X` 表示矩阵中的“非零”元素（其绝对值的平方大于或等于 $10^{-5}$ 的复数），`.` 表示矩阵中的“零”元素（其绝对值的平方小于 $10^{-5}$ 的复数）。

矩阵的行索引和列索引采用小端格式：索引的最低有效位存储在量子比特数组的最前面。因此，矩阵的第一列给出了将酉操作作用于 $|00..0\rangle$ 基态后所得各基态的系数，第二列给出了将其作用于 $|10..0\rangle$ 基态后所得各基态的系数，以此类推。你可以使用 [DumpUnitary 工具](https://github.com/Microsoft/QuantumKatas/tree/master/utilities/DumpUnitary)获取你的酉操作所实现的矩阵的系数（不考虑列之间的相对相位），以及相应的 `X` 和 `.` 的排列模式。

你需要实现一个操作，它接收一个包含 $N$ 个量子比特的数组作为输入，并对其应用具有上述矩阵形状的酉变换。若有多个酉操作满足要求，你可以实现其中任意一个。你的操作的“输出”是其所实现的矩阵系数的排列模式；你可以在 [UnitaryPatterns](https://github.com/Microsoft/QuantumKatas/tree/master/UnitaryPatterns) kata 中查看测试框架。

你的代码应具有以下签名：

```
namespace Solution {
    open Microsoft.Quantum.Primitive;
    open Microsoft.Quantum.Canon;

    operation Solve (qs : Qubit[]) : Unit {
        // your code here
    }
}
```

不允许在你的操作中使用测量。
